items.name: AuthProvider
items.description:
Authentication provider: the one sign-in session of the app. It runs the
session requests itself (sign in and out, register, password reset, the
current user), decides how every other request carries the credentials
(`authorizeRequest`) and what a failure means (`onError`). Data providers
never handle credentials: they send through the HttpClient that asks it.

items.name: createHttpClient
items.description:
The one request path of Lumi. Data providers, uploads, the agent, the live
stream and the auth provider's own sign-in requests all go through a client:
it asks the auth for the request's credentials (`authorizeRequest`), adds
the locale and tenant, encodes JSON, refreshes once on a 401 and turns a
non-2xx answer into a `DataProviderError`. The data layer passes a signed
client's failures to the auth's `onError`; an unsigned one's to the caller.

All of that is for the client's own backend: `baseUrl`, the page's site and
`trustedOrigins`. A full URL to anywhere else is sent plain, so a page that
names a foreign address never carries the reader's credentials there.

fields.description:

tenant and JSON encoding: add or rewrite headers, sign the method, URL and
body. Runs again for the resend after a 401 refresh. Change the request in
place or return a new one.

decrypt it, or reshape it. Return another Response to replace it; throw to
fail the request.

or the hooks, and its 401 does not sign the reader out.

items.name: createSimpleAuthProvider
items.description:
The session conventions a JSON backend most often speaks. Bearer mode:
login returns a token plus the user and permission list, `me` restores
them. Cookie mode: the server keeps the session in a cookie and `me` says
who is signed in. Permissions read as `resource:action` (`orders:*`, `*:*`).
One session feeds both the auth and access providers, so a JSON-configured
base needs no code for it; its own requests go through an HttpClient it
signs itself. Session requests (login, logout, refresh) carry whatever
session there is and never trigger a refresh.

items.name: MutationMode
items.description:
When a write shows on screen. `pessimistic` waits for the server;
`optimistic` changes the cached lists and records at once and puts them
back if the server refuses; `undoable` does the same and waits
`undoableTimeout` before sending, offering Undo on a notice meanwhile.

members.name: mutationMode

Updates and deletes only: `optimistic` shows the change at once and rolls
it back on failure; `undoable` also waits `undoableTimeout` with an Undo
notice before sending (Undo rejects with MutationUndoneError, unreported).
Defaults to the context's `mutationMode`, else `pessimistic`.

items.name: PackedDocument
items.description:
Packed documents: a page, manifest or theme sent as `{ "packed": "…" }`
instead of readable JSON, so its text does not show in a browser's network
panel. The value is the JSON text, raw-deflated, masked with a key when one
is set, and written as base64.

This hides a document from a casual look, nothing more: the browser unpacks
it, so a reader who steps through the page still reaches it. What a reader
must not learn has to stay on the server.

sent `{ filters, sorters, columns, format, ...meta }` and answers the file
as a stream, in any format. Without it the records are loaded page by page
and the file is written in the browser.

members.description:

`default` stands for the mounted panel's own backend.

the reader's credentials, locale and tenant.

An entry may instead give only `{ onRequest, onResponse }`: the provider
the config already builds for that name keeps its address and gains the
hooks. On the panel's backend they reach every request to it, sign-in,
uploads, the agent, the event stream and served pages included.

Regenerates the variant rows for `attributes`, carrying the entered price,
stock and fields over from `previous` where a combination survives. A row
whose attribute set changed inherits from the closest old row that agrees on
every shared attribute; the `sku` code is only inherited once, so codes stay unique.

items.name: composeAdminExtensions
items.description:
Merges extensions in order: components join the Admin catalog and registry,
maps (handlers, data, auth and access providers, drawers, badges, upload and agent options)
merge key by key, lists (routes, assistant commands and @ tabs) concatenate — a command or tab with
the same value replacing the earlier one — every `onEvent` and
`onWorkspaceChange` listener is kept, and any other option is taken from
the last extension that sets it. A component, action or data provider name
registered twice is reported, and the later one wins; a handler named like
a built-in Admin action (`navigate`, `openDrawer`, `closeDrawer`) is refused
when the Admin is created.

items.name: LumiFunnelChart
items.description:
A centred funnel drawn in SVG: each stage is a band whose width tapers down
the funnel, and trapezoid connectors join consecutive bands into one
silhouette. The bands step from the full palette colour to a lighter tint;
the connectors carry the stage-to-stage conversion. Names and counts sit in
aligned side columns (above each band in a narrow card), and an ordered list
gives screen readers every stage with its share, conversion and drop-off.

items.name: MountAdminExtensions
items.description:
Everything JSON cannot carry, supplied by a compiled host or by a page script
(`window.LumiAdminSetup`): callbacks, components and providers. A provider
set here replaces the one built from the config: an auth provider signs in
against a backend that does not speak the simple convention, and every
request (data, uploads, agent, live) carries its credentials. `upload` and
`agent` options merge over the defaults.

members.name: dataProviders
members.description:
Data providers by `data` name, reached with `dataProviderName`;
`default` stands for the mounted panel's own backend.
Build them on the `http` the extension context hands over, so they carry
the reader's credentials, locale and tenant.

An entry may instead give only `{ onRequest, onResponse }`: the provider
the config already builds for that name keeps its address and gains the
hooks. On the panel's backend they reach every request to it, sign-in,
uploads, the agent, the event stream and served pages included.
